grants.name: Conservation Partners Grants
grants.amount: $2,000 - $15,000 per year for up to 3 years (up to $2,000 per year for Land for Wildlife and wildlife refuge holders)
grants.description: Ongoing grants for landholders with a private land conservation agreement to carry out management works such as weed and pest control, fencing and revegetation. Applications are accepted year-round while funds last.
grants.eligibilityDetails: Landowner (Australian citizen or registered company, registered for tax with an Australian bank account) holding a qualifying agreement: in-perpetuity conservation agreement, Trust or Registered Property Agreement, wildlife refuge, Wildlife Land Trust or Land for Wildlife. Agreements already receiving BCT annual management payments and offset agreements are excluded.
grants.assessmentCriteria: Need shown in the management plan, value for money, and a sound approach that maintains or improves conservation values.
grants.notes: One of the few grants she can apply for as an individual, if she or a partner landholder near Breeza holds a conservation agreement or joins Land for Wildlife; could fund revegetation with her own native plants.

grants.name: Indigenous Advancement Strategy - Community Initiated Proposals
grants.description: An ongoing, non-competitive pathway to propose projects that meet a need of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. You discuss the idea with a NIAA regional office, submit an initial proposal, and may be invited to apply in full.
grants.eligibilityDetails: Communities, organisations, businesses and individuals may approach NIAA. The proposal must be developed with the Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander community it affects. NIAA generally won't fund what another program can cover. Full eligibility is in the Agency Collaborates (Non-Competitive) Guidelines.
grants.assessmentCriteria: Fit with the Agency Collaborates guidelines, regional strategies and program priorities.
grants.notes: No closing date; suits co-designed knowledge-sharing events on Country with Gomeroi/Kamilaroi Traditional Owners and farmers, ideally with a local Aboriginal organisation.

grants.name: Strengthening Rural Communities - Prepare & Recover (Round 31)
grants.description: Grants for community-led projects that help rural communities prepare for climate impacts or recover from past disasters. Projects that recognise First Nations knowledge are prioritised.
grants.eligibilityDetails: Australian not-for-profit with an ABN or Incorporation Certificate, or a group auspiced by one. DGR not required. Individuals, sole traders and businesses cannot apply. One application across SRC streams per round. Closes 5pm AEDT.
grants.assessmentCriteria: Clear project, readiness and capacity to deliver, community support and partnerships, realistic budget.
grants.notes: Strong fit for drought and flood resilience field days bringing Traditional Owners and farmers together; apply through her Landcare group or another auspicing NFP.

grants.name: Strengthening Rural Communities - Small & Vital (Round 31)
grants.amount: Up to $10,000 (Leverage grants up to $50,000 in targeted areas)
grants.description: Flexible small grants for community-led projects benefiting remote, rural and regional communities, with environmental sustainability as one of the focus areas.
grants.eligibilityDetails: Australian not-for-profit with an ABN or Incorporation Certificate, or auspiced by one. DGR not required. Sole trader and private business projects are ineligible. Priority to communities under 15,000 people. One application across SRC streams per round. Closes 5pm AEDT.
grants.assessmentCriteria: Clear project details, community need and support, realistic budget with quotes, capacity to deliver.
grants.notes: Good for a native plant propagation workshop or Landcare event in Breeza via an auspice; the program page also shows an old 17 Sept line, but FRRR's funding calendar confirms 3 Dec.

grants.name: Environmental Education Grants Program 2026-27
grants.description: Funds education projects that change people's behaviour and practices to improve on-ground environmental outcomes, through co-designed engagement, partnerships and measured impact.
grants.eligibilityDetails: Incorporated associations, community and not-for-profit groups, councils, universities, Local Aboriginal Land Councils, registered NSW Aboriginal Corporations and companies limited by guarantee. Individuals and for-profit businesses cannot apply. Closes 11:59pm via the Grant Management System.
grants.assessmentCriteria: Must address a Trust priority such as Healthy Country and Aboriginal knowledge or restoring ecosystems; judged on behaviour change, skills, partnerships and impact.
grants.notes: Fits a multi-year farmer and Traditional Owner knowledge-sharing program; partner with a Landcare network or Local Aboriginal Land Council as applicant.

grants.name: Rebuilding Futures
grants.description: Funds community-led disaster recovery, prevention and preparedness projects in rural communities affected by declared disasters or extreme weather.
grants.eligibilityDetails: Not-for-profit with an ABN or Incorporation Certificate, or auspiced. Individuals, sole traders and businesses cannot apply. The previous round required a government disaster declaration between Jan 2019 and Dec 2024; check the new guidelines.
grants.assessmentCriteria: Outcomes in at least one resilience dimension such as networks, information, local decision making or resources.
grants.notes: Opening soon; dates are from FRRR's funding calendar as the program page still shows the old round. Possible fit for flood-resilience work in the Gunnedah area via an auspice.

grants.name: Aurizon Community Giving Fund 2026
grants.description: Cash grants for projects in health and wellbeing, community safety, environment and education in communities where Aurizon operates.
grants.eligibilityDetails: Not-for-profits with Item 1 DGR status; project must be in an Aurizon operating area (check the eligible locations map for Gunnedah). Closes 5pm AEDT.
grants.assessmentCriteria: Must fit at least one focus area; see guidelines on the page.
grants.notes: Closes in days; only worth it if a DGR partner such as a Landcare network can apply and the Gunnedah rail corridor is on the eligible map.

grants.name: Environmental Grant Program (Leard Forest Precinct Environmental Trust)
grants.funder: Leard Forest Precinct Environmental Trust via Narrabri Shire Council
grants.description: Funds projects that protect or enhance the environment, such as weed control, habitat improvement, wildlife water stations and water tanks. Due dates are 30 April and 15 October each year.
grants.eligibilityDetails: Applicant groups need not be local, but works must be within 25 km of the Leard Forest near Boggabri and benefit the wider community.
grants.assessmentCriteria: Enhances, protects and provides a sustainable solution for the environment.
grants.notes: Only if partnering on a revegetation or habitat project near Boggabri; next due date after this is 30 April 2027.

grants.name: Our Country Our Future
grants.description: Ongoing national funding for First Nations groups to acquire, manage or develop land and water interests, plus planning and capability projects, via an EOI then application.
grants.eligibilityDetails: First Nations groups only; full criteria are in the program Introduction Pack.
grants.assessmentCriteria: ILSC investment priorities and funding parameters.
grants.notes: Usable only through a Traditional Owner partner; she could be a delivery partner on a Gomeroi-led caring for Country or native nursery project.

grants.name: Public Donations (October-December 2026 quarter)
grants.description: Quarterly council donations for community, sporting and educational groups to run events and functions.
grants.eligibilityDetails: Community, sporting and educational groups; activity must benefit the Moree Plains community.
grants.assessmentCriteria: Greatest community benefit and alignment with Council's Community Strategic Plan.
grants.notes: Only for a field day or knowledge-sharing event held in the Moree Plains area with a local partner group.
